verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.110 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 177. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: Inverse Trigonometric Functions is an SAQ-ONLY unit — the paper gives it only Section B — so the section is fixed by the unit, not inferred. Printed appearances: AP 19. Prove the two positive terms add to the third, and the difference is then zero by inspection. Working with the whole left side at once is far harder. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Quote the addition formula
steps.margin_note: First mark. Tan⁻¹x + Tan⁻¹y = Tan⁻¹((x+y)/(1−xy)) holds when xy < 1. Here xy = 1/91, so the condition is met.
lines: Tan⁻¹x + Tan⁻¹y = Tan⁻¹((x + y)/(1 − xy)), when xy < 1

recall.must_convey: That the addition formula is quoted and the condition xy < 1 is checked, with xy = 1/91.
accept: quote the addition formula and check that x y is less than one, here it is one over ninety one
the formula holds when the product is less than one
state the formula and verify the condition first
formula rasi x y less than one ani check cheyyali
check the condition before using the formula

steps.why: The formula has a DIFFERENT right-hand side when xy > 1 — a π has to be added. Checking the condition is what makes this version valid.
common_mistakes: Using the formula without checking xy < 1.

steps.label: Substitute the values
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Put x = 1/7 and y = 1/13 into the formula and write both parts over 91.

accept: substitute one seventh and one thirteenth and write both parts over ninety one
the numerator is thirteen plus seven over ninety one and the denominator is ninety one minus one over ninety one
put the values into the formula
values substitute chesi ninety one meeda rasali
substitute into the addition formula

steps.why: Putting both the top and the bottom over 91 means the 91s cancel in the next step. Combining them separately makes the same cancellation harder to see.
common_mistakes: Adding the fractions without a common denominator.

steps.label: Simplify to Tan⁻¹(2/9)
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The 91s cancel, leaving 20/90 — which reduces to 2/9.

recall.must_convey: That the 91s cancel to give Tan⁻¹(20/90) = Tan⁻¹(2/9).
accept: the ninety ones cancel leaving twenty over ninety which reduces to two ninths
twenty by ninety is two by nine
the sum of the first two is tan inverse of two ninths
ninety one cancel avthundi, twenty by ninety ante two by nine
simplify to two ninths

steps.why: 20/90 reducing to exactly 2/9 is the whole point — it matches the third term in the question, which is what makes the difference zero.

steps.label: Subtract the third term
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The first two terms equal the third, so subtracting it leaves 0.

recall.must_convey: That the first two terms equal Tan⁻¹(2/9), so subtracting the third gives 0.
accept: the first two add to tan inverse of two ninths so subtracting the third gives zero
the two sides cancel leaving zero
the left hand side is zero
modati rendu third term tho same, teesthe zero
subtract and close

steps.why: The proof works because the sum of the first two IS the third — the statement is an identity, not a coincidence of decimals.
common_mistakes: Trying to combine all three terms at once.
Stating the answer without showing the subtraction.
